content.text: I reviewed all input files, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs, and built a full source ledger.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. I checked all 17 claims (three independent: apparatus claim 1, installed-assembly claim 11, method claim 14, plus dependents 2-10, 12-13, 15-17) limitation by limitation, all 28 entries in the numeral ledger (10-66, with 28 unused), every numbered part as used in the description, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the abstract (146 words, within the 150-word limit), and all five figure briefs, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which duplicates the disclosure and truncates mid-sentence at "To remove the clamp, releasing"). input/brief.md was used only for title/applicant/inventor/priority/government-support formalities; the YOU passage in the conversation (which asserts a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface") was treated as context only, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft text. Traced and confirmed supported: the two semicircular frame halves, hinge end and opposite latch end, the three jaw carriages in radial guides, the pivoting concave jaw pads and the "without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter" result, the carriage springs biasing outward and retracting the pads on release, the segmented cam ring in the annular guide with one segment carried by each frame half, the complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces that couple on closure and separate on opening, the followers in oblique slots, the wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face, the limited stroke, the synchronized/equal inward travel, the first holding position and second over-center position, the force-limiting spring stack in the drive path between latch handle and wedge taking up remaining travel, the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and its "does not measure pipe diameter" limitation, the mounting boss outside the annular guide for a sensor, tool or conduit and its non-participation in synchronization, the install and remove sequences, and reusability. Internal consistency checks passed: claims and description use the same relationships and terms ("ring drive face" is consistently distinguished from the coupling "drive faces"); every numeral designates exactly one part; the union of the five figure numeral sets exactly equals the ledger and every ledger numeral appears in the description; FIG-1/FIG-2/FIG-3 agree on hinge at the left break, latch at the right break/junction, first (upper) half and segment versus second (lower) half and segment, and carriage/slot positions at top, lower left and lower right; FIG-4 expressly declares its rotation relative to FIG-1, so the handle direction is not a conflict; no section lines are designated in any view, so no repeated section designation is at issue; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Figure-brief geometry choices for parts whose appearance the inventor did not describe (housing outline, wedge block, pad blocks, zigzag springs, boss projection, abutting end-face outlines) are confined to the briefs, are declared schematic, and add no untraced functional relationship; the circumferential position of ring drive face 54 near the latch-end junction and the shared rotational sense of the three oblique slots are functional consequences of the disclosed latch-carried wedge and of synchronized inward travel, so they are traced rather than invented. One defect was found: the description's orientation paragraph verbalizes a pipe-to-frame coaxiality relationship the inventor never states, which is exactly the pattern of a depiction convention escaping the figure brief into the application text. Detail and a delete-only fix are given below. Prior-art characterizations in the Background were left for the later citation trace; the art supplied may be incomplete.

findings.title: Description asserts the frame axis is substantially coincident with the pipe axis, a relationship the inventor never discloses
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, opening orientation paragraph (first paragraph, final clause)
findings.detail: The application text states that the central axis of the closed frame "in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped." This is an affirmative technical relationship (the clamp centers the pipe on the frame axis), not a mere naming convention for the words inward/outward/radial/circumferential. The disclosure never says the pipe is centered on, coaxial with, or concentric to the frame; it says only that three carriages are "distributed around the closed frame," that the slots produce "synchronized inward travel," and that the pivoting pad "bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter." The only place the pipe/frame axis relationship is discussed anywhere in the file set is the drafting agent's own Background prose criticizing prior art ("the pipe is pushed away from the axis of the frame"), which is candidate prose and prior-art characterization, not inventor support. FIG-1's instruction to draw the frame body "concentric with the pipe circle" is an acceptable depiction convention only so long as it stays inside the figure brief and the application text and claims remain neutral on the pipe axis; here the convention has been verbalized in the description, which adds an undisclosed relationship to the embodiment. The claims are unaffected (claim 1 recites only a frame that "surrounds a central axis"; claim 11 recites a pipe but no coaxiality), so the clause can be deleted with no claim-support consequence.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped." Nearest source passages (input/disclosure.md), which show the gap: "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame." and "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages." and "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter." No affirmative passage in the disclosure or in the USER passage of input/conversation.md states any coincidence, concentricity, or centering relationship between the frame axis and the pipe axis.
findings.fix: Delete the untraced clause only, leaving the sentence as: "Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame." Make no other change; do not add a substitute statement about pipe centering, concentricity, or an alternative axis relationship anywhere in the application text, and leave FIG-1's brief as written so the concentric depiction remains a figure-level convention.
